gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-mada: Wire-bent lowercase, every stroke drawn with one unbroken, unwavering gauge. Mada has curves that refuse to close and a towering midzone, so paragraphs of text move along easily beneath Edo SZ.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-mozilla-text: Constant pen pressure, with lowercase built like cast iron. Edo SZ does its best work in a brief, large headline, while Mozilla Text lets its flared terminals and bold-looking lowercase carry the reading.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Thick wire bent into letters, straight through every word. Edo SZ is built for bold, striking display lines, whereas Noto Sans Armenian offers full, standing lowercase and wide, inviting round letters for sustained text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Edo SZ has no hairlines at all, so each stem matches every other stroke from the first letter to the last. Made small, Edo SZ loses punch; Noto Sans Chakma keeps its open mouths.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Flat, unmodulated strokes give Edo SZ its look, while Noto Sans Deseret brings open apertures and a wide-looking lowercase. Paragraphs here would read smoothly, with squat ascenders staying out of the way.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Noto Sans Elbasan brings large lowercase forms and open terminals that never pinch shut beneath Edo SZ's constant stroke. Edo SZ is at home on a single short, large display line.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Strokes that look traced with a marker give Edo SZ its constant, unhurried line. And Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of its height with lowercase, its open terminals keeping words clear, leaving Edo SZ the display lines.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Edo SZ is monoline through and through, its lowercase made for display. But Noto Sans Khojki is the one for text, with exits wide enough to pass light and a clear, large eye on every e.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Edo SZ looks like thin steel rod bent into every letter, with a lowercase that stands up to capitals. Noto Sans Mahajani has a funnel-shaped e that lets text slip by smoothly.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Edo SZ keeps its strokes uniform and its lowercase stately, while Noto Sans Mandaic climbs close to its capitals. The unclamped curves of Noto Sans Mandaic are the real draw.
